body:
## What this does

`merge-on-approval.yml` now passes `--subject "<PR title> (#<number>)"` on a squash merge, so the subject of the single commit that reaches `main` is **set**, not inferred.

Before this, the landing subject was *predicted* from the repo's `squash_merge_commit_title` setting plus the PR's commit count: GitHub's default `COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE` uses the commit's own subject on a single-commit PR and switches to the PR title from two commits up. The bump-token guard had to reproduce that inference to know what it was guarding, and the docs had to tell contributors "put the token in both places, because it depends".

Passing the subject deletes all of that: the single-commit branch, both API reads (`squash_merge_commit_title` and the commit count), and the "both places" rule. One rule remains — **the bump token goes in the PR title.**

## Why this is a MAJOR, deliberately

This is intentional, not a mis-classification, and it is the point most worth reading before approving.

The repo's rubric says "if a caller's shim could keep working untouched → patch or minor". Every shim *is* untouched — no input, secret or permission changes. By that line alone this would be a minor.

It ships as a major anyway because it changes observable behaviour for every caller **with no opt-out**: a caller on GitHub's default whose PRs are single-commit currently lands that commit's own subject, and after this lands the PR title instead. That is "changing a default callers must react to".

An opt-out input (`squash-subject: pr-title|repo-default`, defaulting to today's behaviour) was considered explicitly and declined. It would keep *both* code paths alive — the controlled one and the inferred one — and the inferred path is precisely the complexity this change exists to delete. A `repo-default` default would also force the guard back to reading `squash_merge_commit_title` and the commit count, which is the per-repo dependency being removed.

Consequence, accepted knowingly: cutting v6 **freezes v5**, because `tag-release.yml` re-points only the current major. Every caller keeps running v5 code until its `uses:` is moved by hand.

## The mirror hazard, and what is done about it

Forcing the subject closes "the bump token was lost" and opens "the bump token was gained". Because the PR title is now always the landing subject, a token written there incidentally — quoting an error, naming the convention in prose — cuts that release for real.

`tag-release.yml` excludes commit **bodies** for exactly this reason: prose discussing a bump once matched itself and cut a spurious release. That mitigation cannot transfer here, because under this convention the title is the only channel the token can travel on, so an incidental token and an intended one are byte-identical and no check can separate them.

Since no check can, the guard does the one thing available: on **every** squash — not only when a bump was requested — it logs which release the merge will cut, at the point where the fix is still free (edit the title, no new commit, the approving review survives).

## What is deliberately NOT in this PR

Two files stay pinned at `@v5`, both for reasons recorded in `CLAUDE.md`:

- **`pr-merge.yml`** — a `uses:` job validates against the PINNED ref, and `@v6` does not exist until this merge cuts it. Rolling it here would be `startup_failure` and the PR could not land itself.
- **`pr-checks.yml`** — it names itself in its own `paths-ignore`, so a PR changing only it creates no run at all, and bundling it with another path yields a run that exists but reviews nothing.

Until both are repointed, **this repo's own merges keep running frozen v5**, so the `--subject` behaviour documented here is not in effect for this repo's own automation. Tracked in **#43**, which is blocked on the v6.0.0 tag this PR cuts.

## Testing

The guard's shell is extracted verbatim from the YAML by index and run against a stubbed `gh`: **11 cases, 4 of them positive controls.** Flipping the comparison turns exactly those 4 red. The stub's catch-all `exit 99` is never reached, which is the positive evidence that the two removed API reads are genuinely gone rather than merely unused.

## Scope of the v6 roll

Every documented pin moved to `@v6`: README usage examples, `SECURITY.md`, the PR template, the k8s and runner-image READMEs, doc-comment examples, and the three real intra-repo `uses:` lines in `release-extension.yml`. A byte-level inventory (not code search, which measured ~12% recall on this enumeration) puts the remaining work at **20 active repos, 73 files, 92 floating `@v5` refs**; the three `@v4` stragglers are all archived and stay as they are.
